title: The metrics that counted half a batch
blurb: Partial batches and full-shard retries corrupted rollups.
prompt: Dashboards showed traffic dipping every night around deploys, because batch merges were per-sample and a crash applied half a batch, while retries re-sent windows to shards that already accepted them. The model-generated draft has no atomic merge and no window dedupe. Review it, fix it, and prove merges are whole and retries are per-shard.
aiNote: The draft merges each sample with its own INCRBY, so a crash leaves a silently partial batch, and when one shard fails it retries every shard, double-counting windows that already succeeded because nothing dedupes by window id.
testIdea: Crash mid-batch and assert the window contains either all deltas or none; fail one shard and assert only it is retried with the same window id; query a 9-day range and assert 400.
followUps: How do you bound label cardinality without breaking useful dimensions?
What downsampling policy keeps dashboards honest?
How would you replay a rollup from the raw stream?
